verdicts.bypass: With the API booted under NODE_ENV=production / BILLING_ENABLED=false / STRIPE_DRIVER=none and REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6399 (nothing listening), five request paths still return HTTP 500 with the identical "Stream isn't writeable and enableOfflineQueue options is false" stack the finding names. Two are authenticated tenant READS, which is the explicit acceptance criterion: GET /t/auditlib/billing -> 500 at PlatformSettingsService.billingEnabled (platform-settings.service.ts:34, reached from BillingService which calls settings.billingEnabled() unguarded at billing.service.ts:225/257/273/300); GET /t/auditlib/announcements/active -> 500 at AnnouncementDeliveryService.activeForUser (announcement-delivery.service.ts:71). Also GET /t/auditlib/catalog/isbn-lookup/9780140328721 -> 500 at IsbnLookupService.readCache (isbn.service.ts:52), POST /auth/password-reset/request -> 500 at PasswordResetService.request (password-reset.service.ts:72), POST /auth/verify-email/resend -> 500 at EmailVerificationService.send (email-verification.service.ts:83). Reproduced identically two ways: cold boot against a dead Redis port, and `redis-cli -p 6390 shutdown nosave` under a live API.
verdicts.reasoning: The half the finding is titled after IS fixed and I proved it twice. With Redis unreachable: /healthz 200, /readyz 503 with the DESIGNED diagnostic body {"redis":false,"controlDb":true} (not the generic 500 envelope), /metrics 200, /system-mode/current 200, /admin/system-mode/current 401 (guard reached, not 500). SystemModeMiddleware now calls resolveGlobalSafe() and SystemModeService/TenantResolverService/EffectivePlanService readCache+writeCache are try/catch fail-open with a bounded FailOpenMemo. Core circulation survives: login 200, POST /t/:slug/catalog/books 201, signup 201, members/loans/reservations/library/settings all 200. I also checked the fail-open cannot point the wrong way: with Redis dead and a tenant-scoped maintenance row live in the control DB, GET /system-mode/current?slug=auditlib correctly returned mode=maintenance,source=tenant and both a write and a read into that tenant returned 503 maintenance — so it degrades to the DB rather than fabricating 'normal'. And it does not hide the outage: /readyz flips to 503 and every degrade logs a warn. But the finding's own `fix` field is explicit that TenantResolverService alone is not enough 'otherwise tenant routes still 500 with Redis down', and the remediation's own comment in effective-plan.service.ts claims 'Guarding at the call site keeps that promise regardless of what the settings service does' — it guarded ONE of five call sites of a method it knew throws, and left four other unguarded Redis call sites on request paths. Any 500 is a refutation; there are five.

verdicts.bypass: Same execution as boot-and-config-01. The billing one is fetched by the tenant home page itself (apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/page.tsx:42) and is the whole content of the /t/:slug/billing screen. No such integration test was added either — `grep -rn 'renderScheduledJobMetrics|toScheduledJobResult' apps infra` shows the new specs are pure-function unit tests; there is no kill-Redis integration test anywhere.
verdicts.reasoning: Probes and the mode resolver are genuinely fixed (see boot-and-config-01 reasoning; /readyz now returns its designed 503+dependencies body instead of a 500 envelope, which is the specific diagnosability defect this finding was downgraded to). But the acceptance criterion is a conjunction and the second half fails on three routes, including the ISBN lookup that backs the barcode-scan / add-a-book flow — a librarian at the desk cannot catalogue a book during a Redis restart, and gets a 500 support code rather than a degraded answer. This is the same shape as the previously-refuted attempt (EffectivePlanService behind PlanGuard), one layer further out.

EXECUTED, not read. (1) Booted apps/api/src/worker.ts under NODE_ENV=production against the live audit control plane with 2 active tenants and a real Redis; the runner's own boot tick produced `[scheduled] member-notifications (41ms): 2 tenant(s) scanned; no member reminders due` with ZERO 'member notifications failed for tenant=' warn lines, and /healthz reported member-notifications counts {dueSoon:0,overdue:0,holdReady:0,tenantsScanned:2,tenantsFailed:0}. Previously this was 100% tenantsFailed on every tick. (2) Called `sendMemberNotifications()` directly with NO context — the exact cold-client shape that used to reject — and got tenantsFailed:0, ok:true. The fix is doubly held: RedisService.ready() awaits the 'ready' event before the first command (with an 'end' listener and a 10s backstop so a genuinely dead Redis fails loudly rather than hanging), AND registry.ts now passes the runner's long-lived client through JobContext. I checked the failure mode is still loud rather than newly silent: with tenant DBs unreachable the same handler reported tenantsFailed=2 and ok=false. I looked for the same cold-client pattern elsewhere: `grep -rn 'new RedisService()'` leaves only worker.ts:161, scheduled-jobs.runner.ts:183 and email-worker.ts:106, all long-lived, and email-worker.ts:107 awaits ready().

EXECUTED at both granularities. (a) Tenant level: pointed every tenant's dbUrl at 127.0.0.1:55999 and ran the real registry handlers through toScheduledJobResult — reservation-pickup-expiry, fine-accrual, book-metadata-refresh and member-notifications all returned ok=false with '…; FAILED — tenantsFailed=2' and the full counts object, and the runner now console.warn()s instead of console.log()ing them. Confirmed end-to-end on a booted worker: /healthz scheduledLastResults showed ok=false + 'FAILED — tenantsFailed=3' on four jobs. (b) The one-level-down lie the previous round flagged as a bypass is also closed: I installed a BEFORE UPDATE trigger raising an exception on the tenant's `reservations` table so only the per-ROW transaction fails, and got `ok=false msg="2 tenant(s) scanned; no pickups to expire; 1 reservation(s) failed; FAILED — rowsFailed=1" counts={...rowsFailed:1}` — previously that exact scenario reported a clean success. The `/Failed$/` suffix convention is opt-out rather than opt-in, and 'failed' is grandfathered for export-cleanup (verified LEGACY_RUN_FAILURE_KEYS contains it). describeError now renders empty-message Prisma errors — the warn lines carry 'PrismaClientKnownRequestError:\n…Can't reach database server at 127.0.0.1:55999' instead of the empty colon the audit caught. I am marking the FINDING fixed because its named defect (tenantsFailed discarded, ok hard-coded true) is demonstrably gone; the metrics/alerting half of its suggested fix was written but never wired, which I report as a separate new problem rather than folding into this verdict.

verdicts.bypass: The Redis defect is fixed but the finding's stated outcome — 'the safety net for failed Stripe webhooks … fails on its first event every 5 minutes' and 'the sweep aborts having retried nothing' — is still literally true in the SHIPPED production configuration, for a third distinct reason. Reproduction: insert `stripe_webhook_events {id:'evt_rj_16', type:'customer.subscription.updated', error:'previous failure'}` into the control plane, then run sweepFailedStripeWebhooks() with NODE_ENV=production, STRIPE_DRIVER=none, BILLING_ENABLED=false (verbatim .env.prod.example + x-app-env). Result: `STRIPE no-ctx THREW: STRIPE_API_KEY is required when STRIPE_DRIVER=real. Set it (e.g. sk_test_…) or switch to STRIPE_DRIVER=fake in development.` Cause: stripe-retry.job.ts:130-131 selects the driver with `env.stripeDriver === 'real' ? new RealStripeDriver() : new FakeStripeDriver()`, bypassing the createStripeDriver()/resolveStripeDriverKind() factory this same diff introduced; config/env.ts:352-359 maps the new shipped value STRIPE_DRIVER=none to 'real' outside development, so RealStripeDriver's constructor throws. Confirmed live on a booted worker: /healthz shows `stripe-webhook-retry ok=false FAILED: Error: STRIPE_API_KEY is required when STRIPE_DRIVER=real`, every 5 minutes, retrying nothing. Note the other branch is no better: STRIPE_DRIVER=fake would construct FakeStripeDriver, which stripe-driver-kind.ts says must never run off a dev/test host.
verdicts.reasoning: The cold-Redis mechanism IS fixed and I proved the lock line is now reached: with STRIPE_DRIVER=real + dummy keys and NO job context (freshly-minted client), the sweep got past `await redis.ready()`, acquired the per-event SETNX lock, dispatched the row, and returned `{message:'retried 1: 0 succeeded, 1 still failing, 0 skipped (locked); FAILED — retryFailed=1; backlog — abandoned=1', ok:false, counts:{considered:1,succeeded:0,retryFailed:1,skipped:0,abandoned:1}}` — no 'Stream isn't writeable' anywhere, and the stillFailing->retryFailed rename plus the 24h give-up budget behave as documented (my 48h-old poison row landed in `abandoned`, which correctly did NOT flip ok). But I cannot call the finding fixed: run it under the configuration that actually ships and the sweep still aborts having retried nothing. Defaulting to false as instructed.

new_problems.issue: The sweep picks its Stripe driver with `env.stripeDriver === 'real' ? new RealStripeDriver() : new FakeStripeDriver()` instead of the createStripeDriver()/resolveStripeDriverKind() factory this same diff introduced. config/env.ts:352-359 only recognises 'real'|'fake' and defaults everything else to 'real' outside development, so the newly-shipped STRIPE_DRIVER=none resolves to 'real' and RealStripeDriver's constructor throws. The stripe-webhook-retry job therefore crashes every 5 minutes, retrying nothing, on any host that has an unprocessed webhook row — i.e. exactly the failure reliability-16 was meant to remove, now permanent rather than intermittent. The else-branch is no safer: it would construct FakeStripeDriver, the driver stripe-driver-kind.ts exists to keep off production hosts.

BUT the password-reset leg — the one the finding called 'locked out permanently', and the only recovery a library OWNER has — does not work for the human it is aimed at. BLOCKER launch-readiness-01' and :974 'Password reset, email verification and staff invites are dead ends with **no operator recovery path**', citing docs/deploy-from-the-server.md:113 — a file now reduced to a 26-line 'superseded' stub. grep -rln 'admin/emails|account-recovery' docs/ returns only a June 2026 audit JSON: the escape hatch is documented nowhere an operator would look. verdicts.reasoning: Proved over HTTP, not by reading. Booted the API (fake driver, NODE_ENV=development so the endpoint verifies) and drove three cases against the audit Postgres. (1) Healthy: signed customer.subscription.updated -> 200, stripe_webhook_events row processedAt set, subscription moved to institutional/sub_probe_ok. (2) DATABASE OUTAGE — pg_ctl -m fast stop, then two signed deliveries: both returned HTTP 503 {'message':'Webhook storage unavailable — please redeliver.'}, NOT 200. After restarting Postgres, neither event had a row (nothing was silently accepted), which is exactly right: no row exists, but Stripe was never told we had it, so it redelivers. This is the executed refutation of the old behaviour, where the same sequence returned 200 and the event was gone. persistEvent (stripe-webhook.controller.ts:216-247) uses create-then-catch-P2002 so it can tell a first delivery from a retry, and reports durable:false both when the insert fails and when the P2002 follow-up read fails — the caller 503s on either. (3) Dispatch failure AFTER the row is on disk: a payload with no `items` -> 200, row left processedAt=null with error='Cannot read properties of undefined (reading data)' — i.e. visible to the sweep, which I then ran and which reported 'retried 1: 0 succeeded, 1 still failing'. So the 200-means-durably-ours contract holds on all three paths. Caveat, filed separately as a new problem rather than as a refutation: the sweep this contract hands off to is dead on any non-'real' posture because jobs/stripe-retry.job.ts:133 builds its driver from env.stripeDriver instead of the posture resolver.
